I bet phrase

I’d be surprised if not

also I bet that …, I shouldn’t wonder if, I wouldn’t be surprised if, most likely, I’ll be bound, ten to one, I dare say

classical

Ter. And. 598: Mīrum nī domī est.
Plaut. Amph. 319: Mīrum nī hic mē quasi mūrēnam exossāre cōgitat.

mīrum nī (+ indicative)

it’s a wonder if … not: I bet …, most likely …

(vōx cōmica: Plaut., Ter.)

Lewis & Short s.v. mīrus: “it would be wonderful, I should wonder, I am very much mistaken, if not, i.e. most probably, undoubtedly”. Also mīrum nisi.

Other words

  • mīra sunt nī (nisi) — the same, in the plural: I’d be surprised if … not

    also used · classical · Plaut. Amph. 283: mīra sunt nisi invītāvit sēsē in cēnā plūsculum; Plaut. Bacch. 450

    (vōx cōmica: Plaut.)

Examples

  • Mīrum nī domī est.

    I bet he’s at home.Ter. And. 598

  • Mīrum nī hic mē quasi mūrēnam exossāre cōgitat.

    I bet he means to bone me like an eel.Plaut. Amph. 319

  • mīra sunt nisi invītāvit sēsē in cēnā plūsculum

    I’d be surprised if he didn’t do himself rather too well at dinnerPlaut. Amph. 283

See also be surprised, probably, bet.

SourcesLewis & Short: mirus

Plautus, Amphitruo 283, 319; Bacchides 450. Terence, Andria 598.
